title: Oboe
summary: Limits first: the reed is assembled, not measured; its mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, none printed. Since the reed's closure stop (a857c6f17) the scale sits -7 to +33 c from equal temperament (F4 at its printed pressure only); before it, 22 to 158 c flat. At the pages' 7.4 kPa F4 plays an octave up (677 Hz). The old flat scale was the reed passing through its lay. The tongue is a labelled borrowed-number row (`tongue_contact`, described near the end) on the Bb4, F4, D5, Ab5 and D4 pages and is not on the Db4 and G5 pages; only the first open hole has a nonlinear loss, a quasi-steady orifice (all eleven open holes on the D5 page, `open_hole_orifice 11`, all five on the F4 page, `open_hole_orifice 5`, and all nine on the Ab5 page, `open_hole_orifice 9`; all three on the D4 page, whose card carries `open_hole_orifice 3`; the Db4 page, on the discontinuous-Galerkin bore, has no orifice law at all), and the breath noise row on Bb4, Db4, D4, F4, D5, G5 and Ab5 drives only 10 to 20 kHz on this reed's 0.87 mm duct. A C major scale and Ode to Joy are up, each note its own render at the pages' 7.4 kPa except F4, at its printed 6865 Pa, on fingerings inferred from Table III of Nederveen and de Bruijn 1967, the one complete oboe tone-hole table this project holds. Bb4 (6 of 15, strict 5, with the contraction, profile, interaction and length rows below) is a graded page re-rendered after the stop, Db4 (7 of 14, strict 4, on the discontinuous-Galerkin bore at its 9.6 kHz design band, below) is a graded page, and Bb4 sounds as B4, 102 c sharp of its name; G5 plays an octave down and has no grade; Ab5 sounds at its written octave, as a period doubling, and has no grade and no count (below); D4, F4 and D5 are first pages at their printed pressures. A staple pressure recovery row (Almeida, Vergez and Caussé 2007; C_P 0.8 and S_c 4 mm^2, one measured reed's two numbers, borrowed; commit b57b46619) is on the D4 and D5 pages: D4, which does not speak at 6178 Pa without it, speaks with it (301.95 Hz, 48 c sharp of D4, on the first staple page; ungraded, a listening page). The D5 page also carries the clarinet's bore air temperature profile (Noreland 2013, measured on a clarinet and borrowed for the oboe, positions rescaled), the mutual radiation impedance of the open holes and the bell, the printed thick-wall hole lengths of Lefebvre and Scavone, and, as a labelled bound trial, a jet contraction row (`contraction 0.611`, the two-dimensional free-streamline bound pi/(pi+2); commit 25b9bc64c): no double-reed value is printed; the card's reed area (2.0 mm^2) is Almeida's printed typical oboe rest area, not their fitted 3.05 to 3.37 mm^2, so the reed they measured passes more flow than the card's (peak 249 to 313 mL/s against 132, and 81 with the row), 0.611 is a borrowed value and not a coefficient of this reed; the channel's unsteady inertance has no printed effective length and is not in the row. With those five rows the page sounded at 578.17 Hz, D5 -27.2 c (from -73.1 c without any of them, and 571.12 Hz, -48.5 c, with the first four), and scored 5 of 14, 3 on the strict ruler, against 4 and 3 for the page without the contraction row: the row brought the spectral flux inside the loose ruler, while the spectral distance, the third-octave envelope, the harmonic levels, the wavelet and cepstral gaps, odd against even and the centroid all widened, and the page was 5.1 dB quieter (96.5 dB SPL against 101.6). The D5 page now carries `open_hole_orifice 11` (commit 43ad828c9; it carried `open_hole_orifice 3` from commit 043f9b8e9 until then): the quasi-steady orifice loss of all eleven open holes (158 to 539 mm from the reed) solved together through the bore, each hole's coefficient from the gas at that hole, with two stated approximations: each orifice sees its own uncoupled radiation load, not the coupled one of the interaction row, and the sound the holes radiate still comes from the linear network, as for the first hole alone; the fully coupled orifice network is not built. With the loss on the first three holes the page sounded at 579.51 Hz, D5 -23.2 c, and scored 6 of 14, 5 on the strict ruler, against 5 and 3 for the page without the orifice row: the pitch came inside both rulers and the spectral flux inside the strict one, the waveform locked slightly less (autocorrelation 0.992 against 1.000), and the page was 0.3 dB quieter (96.2 dB SPL against 96.5); the render took 2.2 times the CPU. Three was the engine's cap on the ports of one network, not a physical choice, so the cap is now twelve and the row takes every open hole: on all eleven the page sounds at 579.77 Hz, D5 -22.4 c, the level and the harmonic levels H1 to H8 are the same to the digit shown (96.2 dB SPL), and the count stays 6 of 14, 5 on the strict ruler, with seven gaps to the recording slightly larger (harmonics-to-noise 1.04 to 1.20 dB, spectral flux 0.78 to 0.92 dB, centroid, spectral distance, envelope, harmonic levels, STFT) and four slightly smaller (wavelet, cepstral envelope, pitch, odd against even); the render takes 1118 s of CPU against 591 s for the three-hole page, far less than the growth of the realized kernels (15 to 143) would give. The same card without the staple row scored 5 of 14, so on D5 the staple row costs one measure (spectral flux) and brings the pitch 15 c nearer the recording. The staple row lowered the count on Db4 (3 to 2) and Bb4 (6 to 5), so those pages stay without it. The contraction row (0.611, the same bound trial as on D5, on the live card with no other row) raised the Db4 count from 3 to 4 of 14 and the strict count stayed at 3: that page sounded at 280.73 Hz, 22.0 c sharp of Db4 and 33.1 c sharp of the recording (the page without the row, 275.08 Hz, was 2.0 c from the recording), so the pitch measure was lost from both rulers and odd against even from the strict one, while the partial frequencies and the attack came inside both rulers and the harmonics-to-noise reading flipped from 27.6 dB below the recording to 14.0 dB above it; the page was 4.8 dB quieter (97.8 dB SPL against 102.6) and the spectral, envelope, harmonic-level and wavelet gaps widened slightly. With `open_hole_orifice 3` as well (the card's only three open holes, 463, 499 and 539 mm from the reed, solved together, with the two approximations named on D5) that page kept 4 of 14, strict 3, at 280.80 Hz, +22.4 c from Db4 and 33.5 c sharp of the recording, 97.7 dB SPL: the row moved almost nothing on this note, and the cause is not known. The transfer-matrix Db4 page (replaced since by the discontinuous-Galerkin page described after it) carried the contraction row with the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes and the printed hole lengths, and not the orifice row: it sounded at 274.99 Hz, 13.8 c flat of Db4 and 2.7 c flat of the recording, and scored 6 of 14, strict 6, against 4 and 3 for the page it replaced (and 3 and 3 for the original page): pitch, odd against even and harmonics-to-noise (41.4 dB against the recording's 40.4) came inside both rulers, while the cepstral envelope, partial trajectory, partial frequency and spectral flux moved slightly farther, and the page was 1.0 dB quieter (96.7 dB SPL against 97.7). The orifice row put on top of those four rows lowered it to 5 of 14, strict 5 (the harmonics-to-noise gap went from 0.92 to 2.81 dB and left both rulers; the cepstral envelope, 15.37 to 16.46 dB, and odd against even, 0.05 to 0.32 dB, were worse and stayed inside; the pitch, 2.69 to 2.59 c, and the level, 96.65 to 96.67 dB SPL, did not move; the render took 1884 s of CPU against 778), so the orifice row stayed off that page, the one oboe page that dropped it from its posted card. The Db4 page now is the discontinuous-Galerkin render at the 9.6 kHz design band (degree 2, 51 elements, wall memory to 9.6 kHz, the twenty chimneys as ducts, a sparse Krylov propagator, the reed as one lumped mode on a penalty contact, the bell and open holes as one computed baffled-piston array, the contraction row and the clarinet's air profile, no printed hole lengths, no orifice): it sounds at 276.58 Hz, 3.8 c flat of Db4 and 7.4 c sharp of the recording (the page it replaces: 2.7 c flat), steady to 0.0 c, 93.2 dB SPL (3.4 dB below), and scores 7 of 14, strict 4, against 6 and 6: spectral distance (26.05 to 12.68 dB) and harmonic levels (15.80 to 9.36 dB) come inside the loose ruler and harmonics-to-noise leaves it, and on the strict ruler odd against even and harmonics-to-noise leave, so the strict count falls from 6 to 4 while the loose count rises by one. It is too clean: harmonics-to-noise 63.4 dB against the recording's 40.4 (the page it replaces read 41.4). The pitch gap grows from 2.69 to 7.38 c, odd against even from 0.05 to 5.90 dB, the partial trajectory from 11.53 to 14.81 dB, the attack from 1.61 to 1.95 (log2) and the spectral flux from 2.04 to 2.25 dB, while the third-octave envelope (20.71 to 8.55 dB), the cepstral envelope (15.37 to 7.98), the wavelet (23.48 to 17.42) and STFT (30.66 to 26.43) gaps and the centroid (13.82 to 8.41 st) shrink; the render takes 11862 s of CPU on ts2. It posts by the loose count, with the strict fall and the too-clean note named on its page. The Bb4 page first carried three of those groups without the staple row: the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes (the doubled hole, holes 8 and 9 at one axial station, is coupled at its touching distance since commit 418a8f86b; before it the engine refused) and the printed hole lengths. It scored 6 of 15 against 6, a tie on the loose ruler, and 4 against 5 on the strict ruler (spectral flux left it), sounded 8.8 c sharper (496.22 Hz) and 0.87 dB quieter, and eight gaps to the recording moved slightly farther, against hundredths gained; with the staple row added it fell to 5 of 15. The Bb4 page now carries the contraction row as well (0.611, borrowed, a bound trial, no staple row, no orifice row): it sounds at 494.45 Hz, 102.0 c sharp of Bb4 and 99.6 c sharp of the recording, and scores 6 of 15, strict 5, against 6 and 4 for the page it replaces and 6 and 5 for the original page: spectral flux comes back inside the strict ruler, while the spectral distance, third-octave envelope, harmonic levels, cepstral envelope, odd against even and centroid move slightly farther, and the STFT and wavelet gaps, the pitch gap (105.8 to 99.6 c), harmonics-to-noise and attack move nearer; the page is 4.0 dB quieter (99.6 dB SPL against 103.6). On the original card the contraction row alone lowered the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4); together with the three groups it ties the loose count and gains a strict measure, so it is on the Bb4 page. The orifice row (`open_hole_orifice 3`, which solves the doubled hole with its neighbour) on the live Bb4 card lowered the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4; spectral flux leaves both rulers). Put on top of the four-row Bb4 page it lowers the count from 6 to 5 of 15 (strict 5 to 4; spectral flux leaves both rulers, 0.95 to 1.28 dB), moves the pitch 13.4 c lower and the level 1.03 dB lower, and takes 498 s of CPU against 222, so the orifice row stays off Bb4, as on Db4. On F4 the staple row alone moved the register edge below the printed pressure (676 Hz, the second register, at 6865 Pa), so the staple row alone stays off F4. The contraction row alone (0.611, on the live card with no other row) keeps F4 in the first register at its printed 6865 Pa and raises the count from 5 to 6 of 15, strict 5 to 6: that page sounded at 352.49 Hz, F4 +16.1 c (the page without the row, 350.37 Hz, +5.7 c), gained the cepstral envelope and the harmonics-to-noise gap (11.5 to 5.7 dB) inside both rulers and lost spectral flux from both, while the pitch gap widened from 5.8 to 16.3 c, the partial-trajectory and attack gaps widened, and the page was 3.3 dB quieter (98.0 dB SPL against 101.3). With `open_hole_orifice 3` as well (the card's first three open holes, 351, 365 and 431 mm from the reed, solved together, with the two approximations named on D5) that page kept 6 of 15, strict 6, at 352.52 Hz, F4 +16.2 c, 97.8 dB SPL: the row moved almost nothing on this note, and the cause is not known. The F4 page now also carries the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes and the printed hole lengths: it sounds at 354.18 Hz, F4 +24.4 c, and scores 6 of 15, strict 6, level with the page it replaces (no measure changes side of either ruler; the original page was 5 and 5): the pitch gap grows from 16.4 to 24.5 c, the spectral distance, third-octave envelope, STFT, partial trajectory, harmonics-to-noise, attack and spectral flux move slightly farther, the harmonic levels, wavelet, cepstral envelope and centroid slightly nearer, and the page is 0.6 dB quieter (97.2 dB SPL against 97.8); the render takes 990 s of CPU against 421 for the page without the orifice row. The F4 page now carries `open_hole_orifice 5` (commit 43ad828c9; it carried `open_hole_orifice 3` from commit 043f9b8e9 until then): the same orifice loss on all five open holes (351 to 539 mm from the reed), solved together; three was the engine's cap on the ports of one network, not a physical choice, so this is a consistency fix. It sounds at 354.19 Hz, F4 +24.4 c, 97.2 dB SPL, and scores 6 of 15, strict 6, level with the three-hole page (no measure changes side of either ruler): the tone moves by 0.05 c, and the level and the harmonic levels H1 to H8 are the same to the digit shown. Four gaps to the recording grew slightly (partial trajectory 19.76 to 19.99 dB, pitch 24.55 to 24.59 c, harmonics-to-noise 6.92 to 6.93 dB, spectral flux 2.36 to 2.39 dB) and four shrank (cepstral envelope, partial frequency, odd against even, centroid); the render takes 1072 s of CPU against 935 s for the three-hole page on the same build. With the staple row and the contraction row together the note also stays in the first register (353.23 Hz) and scores 5 of 15, strict 5, level with the page without them. Ab5 is posted at its written octave with six rows on the card (the sixth, `tongue_contact`, is described near the end): the contraction row (0.611, the bound trial of the D5 page; no staple row), the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes, the printed hole lengths and `open_hole_orifice 9` (all nine open holes, 129 to 539 mm from the reed; until commit 43ad828c9 the page carried `open_hole_orifice 3`, the vent and holes 11 and 12, because three was the engine's cap on the ports of one network, not a physical choice, so the nine-hole row is a consistency fix). It sounds at 817.20 Hz, Ab5 -28.2 c and 35.4 c flat of the recording's 834.08 Hz, where the page it replaces (the card with the vent and the closure stop and none of these rows) sounded an octave down at 411.32 Hz, Ab4 -16.7 c; the strongest line holds 817.20 Hz to 0.01 c across 0.3 to 2.3 s. It is a period doubling and not a clean note: the line at half the frequency, 408.69 Hz, stands 25.3 dB under the pitch line and the waveform repeats at 408.60 Hz (autocorrelation at the pitch's own period 0.461 with the period moving 174 c, against 0.982 and 0.7 c on the page it replaces; at the doubled period 0.957 and 0.5 c); the page is 5.2 dB quieter (99.2 dB SPL against 104.4); the last 0.15 s falls back toward 411 Hz as the blowing pressure releases; and the render takes 820 s of CPU against 159 for the page it replaces and 224 for the same card without the orifice row (the three-hole page took 512 s, and 532 s rendered again on the same build). Against the three-hole page the tone moves +0.16 c, the lock at the pitch's own period goes from 0.462 to 0.461 and the half-pitch line from 25.0 to 25.3 dB under the pitch line; the note is otherwise the same: the same register, the same period doubling and the same level to the digit shown. Without the orifice row the note is not clean either (lines at 835.7, 1262.3, 1671.4, 2489.1 and 2507.1 Hz within 5 dB of each other; autocorrelation 0.877 at 417.84 Hz with the period moving 37 c; 2.3 dB quieter than the page it replaces). Ab5 has no ruler, so there is no grade and no count: its tests are the register against the written note, whether it speaks and locks, and the level against the page it replaces, and the lock, the level and the second series at half the pitch are worse than before. G5 stays as posted, an octave down (398.35 Hz, autocorrelation 0.956 with the period moving 0.8 c). Two trials of the same rows on it are not posted. With the contraction, profile, interaction and length rows the note does not hold one series: the strongest line jumps between about 1193 and 2364 Hz from one 100 ms slice to the next, autocorrelation 0.907 with the period moving 41 c, 2.3 dB quieter. With `open_hole_orifice 3` as well the strongest line holds 783.4 Hz (the written G5) in every slice, but the waveform does not repeat at that frequency (autocorrelation 0.327) and repeats near 394 Hz, an octave down, with autocorrelation 0.743 and the period moving 31 c, against the live page's 0.956, and the clip is 3.9 dB quieter; so the written octave is not reached. G5 has no ruler either, so neither trial is counted. The D4 page now carries, besides its staple row, the clarinet's bore air temperature profile, the mutual radiation of the open holes, the printed hole lengths and `open_hole_orifice 3` (all three of its open holes, 431, 499 and 539 mm from the reed) and the tongue row `tongue_contact` (described near the end), and not the contraction row: added to the staple, profile, interaction and length rows it silences D4 at 6178 Pa, with or without the orifice row (peak 0.03 Pa, lock 0.13), so it stays off D4. The D4 page sounds at 303.78 Hz, more than 50 c sharp of D4 and so nearer Eb4 than D4 (the page it replaces, 301.96 Hz, sat 48 c sharp of D4), steady (autocorrelation 1.000, the period moving 0.1 c), at 101.4 dB SPL, 0.81 dB under the page it replaces (102.2 dB SPL). Its pitch gap to the recording (294.04 Hz) grows from 46.02 to 56.46 c: 10.1 c of the 10.4 c step comes from the profile, interaction and length rows and 0.3 c from the orifice row, which also costs 911 s of CPU against 369 without it and 116 for the page it replaces. D4 has no ruler, so there is no count and no grade, and the page is a listening page. The gaps to the recording that grow, from regrade.py on lib0139: pitch, spectral distance (32.17 to 32.93 dB), third-octave envelope (22.67 to 23.47), harmonic levels (22.84 to 23.10), STFT (38.62 to 38.98), spectral flux (1.02 to 1.44) and harmonics-to-noise (6.35 to 13.03 dB: the page reads 55.3 dB against the recording's 42.3, 13 dB too clean, and about 7 dB of that rise comes from the orifice row, cause not known); the wavelet, cepstral envelope, odd against even, attack and centroid gaps shrink slightly, and partial trajectory and partial frequency do not move. The rows on Ab5 and D4 were rendered together, so what each does alone was not measured there. The tongue is the opt-in `tongue_contact` row (commit d986948c3; Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2009, Eq. 6, the clamped-free cantilever mode's projection of a uniform contact strip at the reed tip) on the Bb4, F4, D5, Ab5 and D4 pages: `tongue_contact 1.12e-5 6.979e-5 0.2 0.1845 0.005`, a pad of 2 mm by this reed's 5.6 mm (2 mm by 13 mm is Li 2016's contact for a clarinet reed, kept in length and set to this reed's width) pressing the reed tip with 0.2 N until 0.1845 s and letting go over 5 ms. The effective area, 6.979e-5 m^2, is this reed's own face, k h0 / pM, fixed by the card's reed row and not borrowed; the 2 mm length, the 0.2 N and the 5 ms (Almeida 2017) are the clarinet's, and 0.1845 s is the blow's 0.15 s start plus 34.5 ms, the alto saxophone tonguing contact time of Hofmann 2012. No oboe tongue is printed, and the 0.2 N is below the 1.24 N that this reed's stiffness takes at its 0.357 mm opening, so by that arithmetic the tongue alone does not close the reed; the render's reed-opening trace was not read. On every one of the five pages the steady tone is untouched (pitch within 0.03 c, level within 0.005 dB, centroid within 0.1 %, harmonics to the digit shown) and the rise comes earlier: the time to half of the steady level falls from 241 to 228 ms on Bb4, 428 to 371 ms on F4, 216 to 210 ms on D5, 200 to 193 ms on Ab5 and 290 to 261 ms on D4, and the waveform parts from the render without the row at 175 to 197 ms and is not phase-locked back afterwards. Bb4, F4 and D5 tie their counts (6 of 15, strict 5; 6 of 15, strict 6; 6 of the 14 with a ruler, strict 5; the same measures inside): the attack gap grows on Bb4 (3.21 to 3.41, log2) and D5 (5.11 to 5.15), whose recordings attack slowly (163 and 259 ms), and shrinks on F4 (2.80 to 2.35; 98 to 71 ms against 14), where the partial-trajectory gap also shrinks (19.99 to 15.96 dB). The build of these pages, K10, is not byte-equal to the earlier pages' clips: the same cards without the row differ from them by -49 to -67 dB re signal after 0.2 to 0.4 s, and on Bb4 part of the grader's change (partial trajectory 10.41 to 13.52 dB, wavelet 31.08 to 31.97, STFT 42.99 to 43.16) is the build and not the tongue. The Bb4, F4, D5, Ab5 and D4 paragraphs above describe those pages before the tongue row; their steady numbers still hold, except F4's, which the lay moved (next paragraph). Ab5 (still a period doubling at 817.20 Hz with the half-pitch line 25.3 dB under; the peak falls from 5.86 to 5.40 Pa and the lock at the pitch's own period goes from 0.459 to 0.461) and D4 (303.78 Hz, 101.4 dB SPL; the gaps to the recording that grow are STFT 38.98 to 39.04, cepstral envelope 12.61 to 12.91, attack 2.43 to 2.64 and centroid 17.52 to 17.57, and spectral flux shrinks 1.44 to 1.31) have no ruler and no count. G5 has no tongue page: the card tried (the contraction card, `g4c`) sounds at 598 Hz with and without the row, neither the written octave nor the posted page's octave down, with the rise 7 ms earlier. The same row with the effective area scaled with the strip (3.278e-5 m^2, modal factor 0.816) was also rendered on Bb4, F4 and D5 and moved the attack the same way and the tone not at all; it is not posted. The measured reed lay (the four optional lay fields of the `reed` row, `reed 0.000357 0.0056 17720 2.2e-5 3464 0.114 5.7437e6 2.0 1.6e-4 0.0`) is on the F4 page: the stiffness 5.7437e6 is Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2012 Table 1's printed clarinet contact stiffness per area, 8.23e10, times this reed's own face, 6.979e-5 m^2; the exponent 2.0, the onset opening 1.6e-4 m (45 % of this reed's 0.357 mm rest opening) and the Hunt-Crossley loss 0.0 are the clarinet pages' values, borrowed; no oboe lay is printed. Tried on top of the tongue row on Bb4, F4 and D5, it raised the pitch on all three (Bb4 494.45 to 497.11 Hz, +9.3 c; F4 354.19 to 356.28 Hz, +10.2 c; D5 579.77 to 589.25 Hz, +28.1 c, as the grader reads them). On F4 it ties the count, 6 of 15 and strict 6 with the same measures inside, so the page posts with it: it sounds at 356.28 Hz, F4 +34.6 c and 34.8 c sharp of the recording (the pitch gap 24.59 to 34.79 c), at 97.7 dB SPL (peak 6.11 Pa, 0.4 dB louder), the harmonics-to-noise gap grows from 6.94 to 7.99 dB, STFT from 40.30 to 41.26, partial trajectory from 15.96 to 16.66 and attack from 2.35 to 2.43, while the centroid (14.88 to 13.81 st), odd against even (6.88 to 5.96), spectral distance, envelope, harmonic levels, wavelet, cepstral and spectral-flux gaps shrink; the lock is 0.984 against 0.950. On Bb4 it was tried and is not posted: the loose count holds (6 of 15) and the strict count falls from 5 to 4 (spectral flux leaves the strict ruler, 0.95 to 1.11 dB), and the pitch gap grows from 99.58 to 108.87 c. On D5 it was tried and is not posted: the count falls from 6 to 5 of 14 and from 5 to 4 on the strict ruler (spectral flux leaves both rulers, 0.79 to 1.35 dB, and the harmonics-to-noise gap grows from 1.46 to 5.03 dB), and the pitch, 12.5 c flat of the recording before, is 15.6 c sharp of it after. The render's reed-opening trace was not read, so why the row lifts the pitch is not shown. The reed channel's viscous slit (`slit_length 0.025`; 25 mm is the clarinet pages' slit length, borrowed as a substitute because no oboe channel length is printed) was tried on the D4 card, which has the staple row and no contraction row (the slit law refuses the contraction): it renders to the end and the note jumps to the second register, 583.5 Hz, D5 -11.4 c, where the card without the row sounds at 303.78 Hz in the first; the series stands on 583.5 Hz (the lines at the odd multiples of 291.75 Hz are 80 to 110 dB under the strongest line, the second harmonic at 1167 Hz), the level is 1.01 Pa rms against 2.34 Pa (7.3 dB quieter) and the peak 5.33 Pa against 13.86 Pa, and the grader refuses the clip as not the named note (the D4 fundamental, 293.7 Hz, is 63 dB under the strongest line). It is not posted, and the slit length was not tuned, since any other length would be an invented one. Eb6 has no render because the printed ladder ends at D5.
physics_present: generic fs-duct conical and cylindrical segments, tone-hole side branches and a flanged bell load, the lumped single-reed owner and the physical baffled outlet receiver already run for the clarinet; a description gives them this bore and a reed with values partly borrowed from the clarinet, and the posted first renders come from it

flow noise at the reed on Bb4, Db4, D4, F4, D5, G5 and Ab5 (Oldham and Ukpoho 1990, extrapolated), with the card's first bore record, 0.87 mm, as its duct radius, by the clarinet cards' rule. At that radius it drives only 10 to 20 kHz, and the code takes the open-area ratio as 0 where this reed's is about 0.8
Fuks and Sundberg 1996 blowing pressures for two professional oboe players are retained as player data

Fingerings chained from Table III's closed and open tones for each hole: inferred, not printed, from C4 to C5 and on the page notes. Where the table prints two rows for a note, the scale takes one and says which; the octave aids, holes 1, 2 and 5, aren't printed and are closed
A rigid, inelastic reed closure stop at zero opening (commit a857c6f17)

Quasi-steady orifice loss at the first open tone hole (all eleven on the D5 page, `open_hole_orifice 11`, all five on the F4 page, `open_hole_orifice 5`, and all nine on the Ab5 page, `open_hole_orifice 9`, commit 43ad828c9; all three on the D4 page, `open_hole_orifice 3`, commit 043f9b8e9): a pressure drop K |U| U with K = rho / (2 C_vc^2 A_h^2), C_vc = 0.61 (c_d 2.69, the free-streamline bound for a sharp edge) and no threshold velocity; on those four pages the holes are solved together through the bore, each hole's coefficient reading the gas at that hole on the continuous field of those cards, with two stated approximations: each orifice sees its own uncoupled radiation load, not the coupled one of the interaction row, and the sound the holes radiate still comes from the linear network, as for the first hole alone (the fully coupled orifice network is not built); no open hole beyond those has one

Staple pressure recovery of the double reed (Almeida, Vergez and Caussé 2007, eqs. 14-17; commit b57b46619), on the D4 and D5 pages: the blade is driven by the pressure drop across the opening and the bore input is raised by C_P (1/2) rho (q/S_c)^2, with C_P 0.8 and S_c 4e-6 m^2, one measured oboe reed's numbers (Figs 14 and 15), borrowed, not this reed's; it neglects the viscous loss along the reed, as this card does

Bore air temperature and humidity profile along the bore on the D5, Db4, F4, Bb4, Ab5 and D4 pages: the CLARINET pages' own continuous gas field, a borrowed shape and not an oboe's (no measured oboe bore profile is held): the exhaled-breath mixture (Coltman 1966, Nederveen 1969) with the 14 stations of the bore air temperature Noreland (2013) measured in a clarinet, 304.15 K and water mole fraction 0.0442 at the barrel to 294.96 K and 0.0257 at the end of the clarinet's 0.655 m bore, only the positions rescaled by 0.634/0.655; it is on the oboe cards because the interaction and printed-length rows below run only on a continuous gas field, and a measured shape is the least invented one held

Mutual radiation impedance between the open holes and the bell on the D5, F4, Bb4, Ab5 and D4 pages (the Db4 page has the computed mutual radiation of its discontinuous-Galerkin bore instead) (TMMI, Lefebvre, Scavone and Kergomard 2013, half-space factor 2), distances along the bore axis only, an upper bound for holes on opposite sides, never less than the sum of the two radii, so Bb4's doubled hole (holes 8 and 9 at one station) is coupled at its touching distance, 4.2 mm (commit 418a8f86b)

Printed thick-wall tone-hole lengths of Lefebvre and Scavone (2012) on the D5, F4, Bb4, Ab5 and D4 pages (not on Db4, whose discontinuous-Galerkin bore has no row for them), in place of the engine's inner length

Vena contracta of the reed jet on the D5, Db4, F4, Bb4 and Ab5 pages (the opt-in `contraction` row, commit 25b9bc64c; the contraction term of fs-phs GapFlowLaw without its channel terms, the staple law, where there is one, taken on the jet area; on Db4, F4, Bb4 and Ab5 the card has no staple row; it is not on D4, where it silences the note): C_c 0.611 = pi/(pi+2), the two-dimensional free-streamline bound, borrowed and a bound trial, not a measured coefficient of a double reed; the card's reed area is Almeida's printed typical rest area (about 2 mm^2), not their fitted 3.05 to 3.37 mm^2, so print does not say it already holds a contraction

Discontinuous-Galerkin bore on the Db4 page (degree 2, 51 elements, viscothermal wall memory with up to 48 poles per wall point from 50 Hz to 9.6 kHz, the twenty tone-hole chimneys as ducts with their own states, a sparse Krylov propagator held to 1e-11 on the full state), the reed as one lumped mode with the same six numbers closing on a penalty contact, and the bell and open holes radiating as one computed baffled-piston array with every mutual term; it replaces the transfer-matrix route on that page and carries neither the printed hole lengths nor the first-hole orifice

Tongue contact on the reed tip on the Bb4, F4, D5, Ab5 and D4 pages (the opt-in `tongue_contact` row, commit d986948c3; Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2009, Eq. 6, the fundamental clamped-free cantilever mode's projection of a uniform strip at the tip): strip 1.12e-5 m^2 (2 mm by this reed's 5.6 mm; the 2 mm is Li 2016's clarinet contact length), effective area 6.979e-5 m^2 (this reed's own face, k h0 / pM, not borrowed), force 0.2 N and release over 5 ms (Almeida 2017, a clarinet), held until 0.1845 s (the blow's 0.15 s start plus 34.5 ms, the alto saxophone tonguing contact time of Hofmann 2012); every number but the effective area is borrowed and no oboe tongue is printed; the reed-opening trace was not read

Measured reed lay on the F4 page (the four optional lay fields of the `reed` row): stiffness 5.7437e6 = Chatziioannou and van Walstijn 2012 Table 1's printed clarinet contact stiffness per area, 8.23e10, times this reed's own face k h0 / pM = 6.979e-5 m^2; exponent 2.0, onset opening 1.6e-4 m (45 % of this reed's rest opening) and Hunt-Crossley loss 0.0 s/m are the clarinet pages' values, borrowed; no oboe lay is printed; it ties the count on F4 and lowers it on Bb4 and D5, so it is on F4 only; it lifts the pitch 9 to 28 c

pad and key heights, undercut geometry and a full fingering chart

a double-reed valve driving this bore at the bands the oboe needs. The typed reed record, the jet contraction row and the constriction_noise row drive the discontinuous-Galerkin bore through the sparse Krylov propagator (the dense propagator's 2048-DOF cap no longer refuses the bore; the sparse cap is 32768 DOF), and the full Db4 at the 4.8 kHz design band renders steady at -3.0 cents. Not in yet: the open-hole orifice and the printed tone-hole lengths are not on the DG route (the live route has both), and nothing above 9.6 kHz is resolved. The open holes' mutual radiation is in the DG radiation operator (a computed baffled-piston array, every self and mutual term), not a row. The staple pressure recovery is an opt-in row on the typed reed: on the DG bore a D4 pilot pair at 6178 Pa speaks with it (0.85 Pa) and is silent without it (0.0017 Pa), no page yet. At the 9.6 kHz design band (degree 2, 48 wall-loss poles) the full Db4 is now the Db4 page: 7 of 14 against the transfer-matrix page's 6 on the loose ruler and 4 against its 6 on the strict one, with the pitch 7.4 c sharp of the recording, the centroid 744 Hz against 1173 Hz and the harmonics-to-noise 63.4 dB against the recording's 40.4 (too clean), and without the printed hole lengths and the first-hole orifice the transfer-matrix page carried. At 20 kHz (degree 3) the bore is refused by a propagator certificate (residual 1.1361e-11 against the card's 1e-11), and the refusing propagator is not the main bore's: its substep loop accepts one substep and all 22 of its port columns converge in 36 to 50 Arnoldi vectors. Which propagator refuses is being measured, and the tolerance was not loosened. The flow-noise row's source (above 8 kHz at this blow) lies above both DG bands tried, so those renders add no audible noise and their harmonics-to-noise stays too clean (70.6 dB at 4.8 kHz, 63.4 dB at 9.6 kHz, against the recording's 40.4)

staple and reed channel geometry (the pressure recovery law is in, with one measured reed's two numbers borrowed; this reed's staple is not measured; the jet contraction row is in, commit 25b9bc64c, with 0.611 borrowed as a bound, since no double reed's contraction is printed, and the channel's unsteady inertance is not in it, since no printed effective length of the channel is held)
a modern specimen: the only complete table is from 1967

A printed pressure for every note: Fuks and Sundberg print one for D4, F4, Bb4, D5 and F5 only, as a range (Table A6, two players, four dynamics, up and down); the pages use the second oboist's ff, rising. F4 (6865 Pa) plays in the first register, with or without the contraction row, and D5 (8041 Pa) speaks; Bb4 at 7551 Pa scored 5 of 15 against 6 and was not posted; D4 at 6178 Pa does not speak without the staple row and speaks with it (with the contraction row added to the staple, profile, interaction and length rows it is silent again); F5 has no printed fingering. G5 and Ab5 are blown at 10.689 kPa (109 cm H2O) and 10.983 kPa (112 cm H2O). Table A6 prints neither note: both values are the linear semitone interpolation between the second oboist's ff, rising-arpeggio F5 (103 cm H2O) and Bb5 (118 cm H2O), 3 cm H2O per semitone, the method used for the A4 value of the description (1 cm H2O = 98.0665 Pa). Every other note uses the pages' 7.4 kPa

The scale's tuning. Before the reed's closure stop the scale was flat because the reed passed through its lay; with it the notes sit -7 to +33 c from equal temperament, F4 plays an octave up in the second register (nothing was done to bring it back), and Bb4 sounds as B4. The reed's blade mass, resonance and face area are borrowed or assumed, none printed: they need the authors or a measured reed

Nonlinear loss at the other open holes (none left on D5, F4, Ab5 and D4, where every open hole carries it; beyond the first on the rest), and a printed coefficient for the first: c_d 2.69 is the code's free-streamline bound, not a printed value (printed: 2 for a tube end, 13/9 for a flanged end and 1.18 for a sharp hole in PVC, the last through a secondary source), and this model's hole edges aren't printed. On Bb4 the second open hole sits at the first one's station and carries the same flow, and the third about 0.6 of it, at the played note (the engine's small-signal transfer, not a render)

An oboe's own bore air temperature profile (the D5, Db4, F4, Bb4, Ab5 and D4 pages borrow a clarinet's), the holes' azimuths (the interaction takes axial distances only), and the spacing of Bb4's doubled hole (holes 8 and 9 at one axial station): the engine couples them at the touching distance, 4.2 mm, an upper bound, because their azimuths are not printed. On D5 the three together moved the steady tone about 11 c and the level under 1 dB against the same card with a constant field, and the grader's count by one measure when the staple row was absent; with the staple row the count is the same as without them

An oboe tongue's own area, force and contact time: the tongue row borrows the clarinet's 2 mm strip length, 0.2 N and 5 ms release and the alto saxophone's 34.5 ms contact time, and sets the strip width to this reed's 5.6 mm and the effective area to this reed's own face; whether the tongue closes the reed was not read (the 0.2 N is below the 1.24 N its stiffness takes at its opening)

An oboe reed's own lay (contact law between the reed and its lay): the F4 page borrows the clarinet's exponent, onset opening and loss and scales the clarinet's printed contact stiffness per area by this reed's face; the other pages keep the default slit lay, because the lay lowered their counts and lifted the pitch
